summary: 失乐症患者的困难可以局限在音乐感知。研究者通过行为和脑结构差异考察这种能力，作者则追问，音乐能力处于连续谱的一端是否就应被视为残障。
logic: 比较音乐和其他听觉能力
讨论差异何时构成残障

paragraphs.brief: 音乐长期以来一直被认为是一个独特的人类概念。
sentences: Music has long been considered a uniquely human concept.
音乐长期以来一直被认为是一个独特的人类概念。
In fact, most psychologists agree that music is a universal human instinct.
事实上，大多数心理学家都认为音乐是人类的本能
Like any ability, however, there is great variation in people’s musical competence.
然而，与任何能力一样，人们的音乐能力也有很大的差异。
For every brilliant pianist in the world, there are several people we refer to as ‘tone deaf’.
世界上每个出色的钢琴家，都有几个人被称为“聋子”。
It is not simply that people with tone deafness (or ‘amusia’) are unable to sing in tune, they are also unable to discriminate between tones or recognize familiar melodies.
不仅音调失聪的人(或“Amusia”)无法唱调，他们也无法区分音调或认识熟悉的旋律。

Such a ‘disorder’ can occur after some sort of brain damage, but recently research has been undertaken in an attempt to discover the cause of congenital amusia (when people are born with the condition), which is not associated with any brain damage, hearing problems, or lack of exposure to music.
这种“病态”可能发生在某种脑损伤之后，但最近已经进行了研究，试图发现先天性动脉的原因(当人们出生时患有这种病症)，而这种病因与任何脑损伤、听力问题或缺乏接触音乐的机会无关。

paragraphs.brief: 正如人们所期待的那样，音乐在歌唱和音乐的节奏中表现得比非音乐要差得多。
sentences: According to the research of Dr. Isabelle Peretz of the University of Montreal, amusia is more complicated than the inability to distinguish pitches.
根据蒙特利尔大学伊莎贝尔·佩雷兹博士的研究，Amusia比无法区分投手要复杂得多。

An amusic (a person who has the condition of amusia) can distinguish between two pitches that are far apart, but cannot tell the difference between intervals smaller than a half step on the Western diatonic scale, while most people can easily distinguish differences smaller than that.
音乐(有马西亚病症的人)可以区分两个相距很远的音轨，但不能分辨西方对音尺度上小于半步的音阶之间的差别，而大多数人很容易分辨比这小的音阶。
When listening to melodies which have had a single note altered so that it is out of key with the rest of the melody, they do not notice a problem.
当听那些音符被改变过以至于它和音符的其余部分都失去关键时，它们没有注意到任何问题。
As would be expected, amusics perform significantly worse at singing and tapping a rhythm along with a melody than do non-amusics.
正如人们所期待的那样，音乐在歌唱和音乐的节奏中表现得比非音乐要差得多。

paragraphs.brief: 由于音乐与语言关系密切，人们可能预计音乐障碍可能是由于语言障碍造成的。
sentences: The most fascinating aspect of amusia is how specific to music it is.
最令人着迷的一面是它是如何与音乐的特殊性。
Because of music’s close ties to language, it might be expected that a musical impairment may be caused by a language impairment.
由于音乐与语言关系密切，人们可能预计音乐障碍可能是由于语言障碍造成的。
Studies suggest, however, that language and music ability are independent of one another.
然而，研究表明，语言和音乐能力是相互独立的。
People with brain damage in areas critical to language are often still able to sing, despite being unable to communicate through speech.
在语言关键地区，脑损伤的人往往仍然能够唱歌，尽管无法通过语言进行交流。
Moreover, while amusics show deficiencies in their recognition of pitch differences in melodies, they show no such deficiencies in tonal languages.
此外，尽管音乐在承认曲调差异方面存在缺陷，但在古代语言中却没有这种缺陷。
Amusics who speak tonal languages, such as Chinese, do not report having any difficulty discriminating between words that differ only in their intonation.
说古代语言的音乐，如中文，并不难于区分在国语上不同的措辞。
The linguistic cues inherent in speech make discrimination of meaning much easier for amusics.
语言的暗示使音乐更容易被区分。
Amusics are also successful most of the time at detecting the mood of a melody, can identify a speaker based on his or her voice and can discriminate and identify environmental sounds.
音乐在发现旋律的情绪、根据自己的声音辨别发言者、区分和辨别环境声音方面大部分时间也是成功的。

paragraphs.brief: 最近的工作重点是确定大脑中造成异常现象的部分
sentences: Recent work has been focused on locating the part of the brain that is responsible for amusia.
最近的工作重点是确定大脑中造成异常现象的部分
The temporal lobes of the brain, the location of the primary auditory cortex, have been considered.
大脑的时间叶，主要的听觉皮层的位置，已经得到了考虑。

It has long been believed that the temporal lobes, especially the right temporal lobe, are most active when engaged in musical activity, so any musical disability should logically stem from here as well.
长期以来人们一直认为，当从事音乐活动时，时间叶，特别是正确的时间叶是最活跃的，因此，任何音乐上的残疾也应从这里产生。

Because it has been shown that there is no hearing deficit in amusia, researchers moved on to the temporal neocortex, which is where more sophisticated processing of musical cues was thought to take place.
既然研究已证明失歌症患者没有听力缺陷，研究人员便转而考察颞叶新皮层，因为人们认为大脑对音乐线索更复杂的处理发生在那里。
New studies, however, have suggested that the deficits in amusics are located outside the auditory cortex.
然而，新的研究表明，音乐中的缺陷位于听觉皮层之外。
Brain scans of amusics do not show any reaction at all to differences smaller than a half step.
脑部对音乐的扫描丝毫没有显示任何反应对小于半步的差异。
When changes in tones are large, their brains overreact, showing twice as much activity on the right side of the brain as a normal brain hearing the same thing.
当音量变化很大时，他们的大脑反应过度，显示大脑右侧的活性是正常大脑听到同样声音的两倍。
These differences do not occur in the auditory cortex, indicating again that the deficits of amusia lie not in hearing impairment, but in higher processing of melodies.
这些差异在听觉皮层中并不发生，再次表明听觉缺陷不在于听力障碍，而在于对旋律的更高处理。

paragraphs.brief: 大部分人都拥有基本的音乐能力，但这并不意味着缺乏这种能力是不正常的。
sentences: So what does this all mean?
这是什么意思？
Looking only at the research of Peretz in the field of neuropsychology of music, it would appear that amusia is some sort of disorder.
仅看佩雷茨在音乐神经心理学领域的研究，似乎阿穆西亚是某种疾病。
As a student of neurobiology, however, I am skeptical.
身为神经生物学的学生，我怀疑。
Certainly the studies by Peretz that have found significant differences between the brains of so-called amusics and normal brains are legitimate.
佩雷茨的研究发现所谓的音乐和正常大脑之间有很大的差别
The more important question now becomes one of normality.
现在更重要的问题变成了一个正常的问题。
Every trait from skin color to intelligence to mood exists on a continuum—there is a great deal of variation from one extreme to the other.
从肤色到智力到情绪的每一个特征都存在于一个连续体上——从一个极端到另一个极端有很大的差异。
Just because we recognize that basic musical ability is something that the vast majority of people have, this doesn’t mean that the lack of it is abnormal.
大部分人都拥有基本的音乐能力，但这并不意味着缺乏这种能力是不正常的。

paragraphs.brief: 是什么让音乐比音乐天才更糟糕？
sentences: What makes an amusic worse off than a musical prodigy?
是什么让音乐比音乐天才更糟糕？

Musical ability is culturally valued, and may have been a factor in survival at one point in human history, but it does not seem likely that it is being selected for on an evolutionary scale any longer.
音乐能力在文化上受到重视，可能是人类历史上某一点上生存的一个因素，但似乎不再有可能被选择为进化型音乐。

Darwin believed that music was adaptive as a way of finding a mate, but who needs to be able to sing to find a partner in an age when it is possible to express your emotions through a song on your iPod?
达尔文认为音乐是适应性的作为一种寻找伴侣的方式，但谁需要能够能够找到一个伴侣在一个时代，当有可能表达你的情绪通过一首歌在你的iPod?

paragraphs.brief: 虽然占卜术的想法很有趣，但它似乎只是内在音乐能力的连续体的一端。
sentences: While the idea of amusia is interesting, it seems to be just one end of the continuum of innate musical ability.
虽然占卜术的想法很有趣，但它似乎只是内在音乐能力的连续体的一端。
Comparing this ‘disorder’ to learning disorders like a specific language impairment seems to be going too far.
将这种“障碍”与学习障碍(如特定语言障碍)相比似乎走得太远了。
Before amusia can be declared a disability, further research must be done to determine whether lack of musical ability is actually detrimental in any way.
在宣布Amusia为残疾之前，必须进行进一步的研究，以确定缺乏音乐能力是否实际上有害。
If no disadvantages can be found of having amusia, then it is no more a disability than having poor fashion sense or bad handwriting.
如果无法发现有马西娅的劣势，那么，它就没有什么比时尚感差或笔迹差的残疾了。

items.en: What does the writer tell us about people with tone deafness (amusia) in the first paragraph?
items.zh: 第一段怎样描述患有失歌症、难以辨别音调的人？
correct: They have several inabilities in regard to music
他们在音乐感知方面有好几种困难。

items.en: What is the writer doing in the second paragraph?
items.zh: 第二段的作者在做什么？
correct: summarising some findings about people with amusia
概述有关失歌症患者的几项研究发现。

items.en: What does the writer say about the relationship between language ability and musical ability?
items.zh: 作家对语言能力与音乐能力之间的关系有何看法？
correct: People who are unable to speak can sometimes sing
无法说话的人有时会唱歌

items.en: In the third paragraph, the writer notes that most amusics are able to
items.zh: 作者在第三段指出，大多数失歌症患者能够……
correct: distinguish a sad tone from a happy tune
区分悲伤的音调和欢乐的音调

items.en: What is the writer doing in the fourth paragraph?
correct: outlining progress in understanding the brains of amusics
介绍人们在了解失歌症患者大脑方面取得的进展。

items.en: Peretz’s research suggesting that amusia is a disorder is convincing.
items.zh: 佩雷茨的研究认为失歌症是一种功能障碍，这一观点很有说服力。
items.why: 作者先介绍佩雷茨的研究似乎支持失乐症是一种障碍，随后明确表示自己对此持怀疑态度，所以并不认为这一推论很有说服力。

items.en: People with musical ability are happier than those without this ability.
items.zh: 有音乐能力的人比没有这种能力的人更快乐
items.why: 文章比较人的音乐能力，并讨论失乐症是否会造成不利影响。文中没有比较有无音乐能力的人谁更快乐。

items.en: It is inappropriate to consider amusia as a real disorder.
items.zh: 把失歌症视为一种真正的功能障碍并不恰当。
items.why: 作者认为，在认定失乐症为残障前，必须先证明缺乏音乐能力确实会造成不利后果。他认为目前直接贴上障碍标签并不恰当。

items.en: People with amusia often have bad handwriting.
items.zh: 失歌症患者的字迹往往比较潦草。
items.why: 作者把字写得不好与失乐症并列，是为了讨论能力差异何时算作残障。类比没有说失乐症患者常常字也写得不好。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: The reason why some people are born with amusia is
items.zh: 有些人天生患有失歌症，其原因……

items.en: One of the difficulties amusics experience is
items.zh: 失歌症患者遇到的一项困难是……
items.answer: C · an inability to follow the beat of music.

items.en: For amusics, discrimination of meaning in speech is
items.zh: 对于失歌症患者来说，分辨话语的含义……

items.en: Certain reactions in the brain of an amusic are
items.zh: 失歌症患者大脑中的某些反应……
items.answer: G · more marked than with other people.

items.en: In most cultures, musical ability is
items.zh: 在大多数文化中，音乐能力是

pairs: 被视为理想特征／受到某种文化重视
题干用名词，定位句改用同词根的副词。
第 4 段 · 第 1 句
第 3 段 · 第 6 句
points: 作者把字写得不好与失乐症并列，是为了讨论能力差异何时算作残障。类比没有说失乐症患者常常字也写得不好。
题干问“在大多数文化中，音乐能力是”。定位句写到“音乐能力在文化上受到重视，可能是人类历史上某一点上生存的一个因素，但似乎不再有可能被选择为进化型音乐”。
clauses: “that music is a universal human instinct”补足 agree 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 agree 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。

An amusic (a person who has the condition of amusia) can distinguish between two pitches that are far apart, but cannot tell the difference between intervals smaller than a half step on the Western diatonic scale, ….
连接词 while 引出“while most people can easily distinguish differences smaller than that”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
